subject: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC

messages.author: 1079648d02bbc376
messages.subject: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC
parts:
Used accelerometer: Movisens (Move 3)

Used GGIR Version: 3.0.1.

Dear all,

I am reaching out to the GGIR community seeking assistance with an issue I've encountered while working with the R package.

During the creation of the Part5 day summary QC, I've run into an error that has proven challenging to troubleshoot. The issue appears to be associated with the loading of data. Specifically, the assignment of the created .RData name consistently lags one ID behind the actual participant (for an example see the picture below).

 Upon closer inspection, removing ID178 temporarily resolves the issue. This has led me to suspect that the problem is rooted in the data associated with this particular participant.

Further investigation revealed that the acc.bin data is missing as a separate entity in the ID178 folder, despite existing in the unisens structure as evident in the .xml data. Interestingly, a separate acc.csv file for this participant is available. I'm wondering if the absence of acc.bin data might be causing the algorithmic discrepancy.

I am reaching out to the GGIR community for insights and potential solutions. Is it feasible to utilize the acc.csv data for ID178 as a workaround? Alternatively, is there a way to independently extract the acc.bin data from the unisens.xml data for this participant?

Note on ID Order: Please bear in mind that the ID order may not align perfectly chronologically due to study dropouts. The correct order should be "176, 178, 181, 183," with ID178 and ID181 missing.

I appreciate your time and expertise, and I'm hopeful that someone within the community might have encountered a similar issue or can offer guidance on resolving this matter.

Thank you in advance for your assistance and if additional information is required to facilitate understanding of this issue, please let me know..

Best regards,

Tim Balder

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC
parts:
Hi Tim,

Thank you for the detailed reporting of your issue. At the moment GGIR is able to read MOVISENS bin files, when I implemented this I only had access to bin files, so GGIR expects a file named acc.bin in your participant folder. I guess this is the problem you are facing. The quick solution for you would be skipping the participants without acc.bin as you are doing and try to read those files with the read.myacc.csv function in GGIR. This is interesting as some years ago movisens did not provide me with a csv file and that's why I had to implement the reading of their bin files.

As for extracting the bin file for these participants, I think you would need to contact Movisens for that.

I am going to try to replicate this issue and make GGIR able to skip the participants in which the acc.bin file is missing. I will get back to you when this is done.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: Assistance Needed: GGIR R Package - Error in Part5 Day Summary QC
parts:
Hi Jairo,

Thank you very much for your quick answer and your continued support! 

I could resolve the error by excluding the individual with missing data, effectively eliminating the issue. To incorporate the ID into the complete dataset, I am going to utilize the "read.myacc.csv" function. Since I'm relatively new to this project and wasn't present during the data collection phase, I'm uncertain whether Movisens typically provides data in the .csv format. However, I'm aware of a method using MATLAB to convert .bin files into .csv, which might prove useful in our context and maybe there is the possibility to convert .csv data back in to the .bin format.

The branch you provided worked seamlessly with our dataset. Your assistance is greatly appreciated!

Unfortunately, we've encountered another error related to the .bin data. Surprisingly, the package failed to retrieve the "acc.bin" data for three specific IDs, despite the data's presence in the folder structure. I conducted a thorough file check, and everything seems to be in perfect order. I'm puzzled as to why the "acc.bin" data isn't being recognized. Any insights or suggestions you may have would be immensely helpful.

Best regards, 

Tim

parts:
Dear Tim,

I am not sure I understand what you did:

  • If there are problems with the movisense file structure and you are not able to read the files with unisensR directly then please reach out to their maintainers. https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unisensR/index.html. It is not helpful for them if we started to develop work arounds without reporting the issue.
  • If you convert bin to csv then make sure you do this for all files and store the csv in a new folder and only use that for your data analysis. Do not mix movisens folders with newly created csv files.
  • If it "does not work" provide a clear reproducible description of the problem. For example, you do not clarify the csv file structure you created and how you attempt to read it with GGIR.

Best regards,

Vincent
